name: Two drawables

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Two drawables

Mechanism: the Metal layer allowed three drawables (`maximumDrawableCount = 3`), each a full-window IOSurface (16 MB at 1280x801 @2x, 33 MB at 4K). The benchmark's frames finish well inside the 8.3 ms interval, so two are enough: set the maximum to 2. Allowed: gpui_apple metal_renderer.rs. Forbidden: presentation or pacing code.
measurementPlanMarkdown: ab.sh over seven scenarios, 3 reps; watch footprint, fps and missed frames (janky_frames). Pass: footprint down about 15 MB everywhere, fps unchanged, missed frames not materially up.

measurements.metric: footprint end MB, fast on (data-table / div-cards / hover-grid / text-relabel)
footprint end MB, fast off (data-table / div-cards / hover-grid)

measurements.after: data-table on 4-8, off 1; animated-dots 1, effects-cards 1 (4 runs of 42)

measurements.delta: within noise; effects-cards on bimodal 2.0/2.65 as before

reportMarkdown:
## Two drawables Finished

Passed: true, with a stated trade. Every scenario drops about 15 MB (9-13%) in both fast modes, a full-window drawable, and more on larger displays. fps and CPU hold; four of the 42 two-drawable runs missed one frame in 600 where the three-drawable runs missed none outside data-table. Two drawables leave the CPU one frame less slack when the GPU runs long, so an application whose frames are GPU-bound near the display interval may prefer three; the setting stays a one-line constant in `MetalRenderer::configure_layer`. Clippy clean; no unit test applies (a layer property).

Attempt Count: 1.
decisionMarkdown:
### Decision

Committed success; reported as a smoothness-for-memory trade.
